subject: Post-call: AcmeHealth private VPC / network & compliance recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Alvarez <sara@acmehealth.com>, Bob Chen <bob.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: AcmeHealth private VPC / network & compliance recap

Hi Sara / Bob —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we have alignment:

Key business drivers you shared
- Must host inference in a customer-controlled VPC (no egress to public internet).
- Data residency: PHI and regulated patient records must stay within US-based regions / your VPC.
- Air-gap option considered for labs with strict network isolation (optional stage).
- Goal: Proof-of-Concept (PoC) in 6-8 weeks to validate latency & throughput on representative workflows.

Primary technical constraints noted
- VPC peering or private endpoints only (no shared subnets).
- Outbound egress strictly controlled - only allow connections to our control plane over a customer-approved IP range OR use a private control plane proxy.
- Strict inbound firewall rules; we may need to provide the acmehealth network team with an IP allowlist and ports.
- KMS integration required for envelope encryption of persistent artifacts; HSM optional.

Security/compliance asks you requested
- SOC 2 Type II report and formal data handling statement.
- Network architecture checklist (NAT, route tables, security groups, proxy settings).
- Audit log retention and access controls.

What we (Redwood) will deliver by EOD Friday:
- High-level Private/VPC architecture PDF that maps to your network checklist (attached).
- Spreadsheet of network requirements (ports, IP ranges, proxy endpoints) for your network team (attached).
- Example mutual action plan and a proposed PoC timeline (2-week staging, 4-week validation).

Next steps / asks from AcmeHealth
1) Please confirm the PoC stakeholder list (apps, infra, infosec) and a preferred PoC start week (target windows: Aug 3 or Aug 17).
2) Share any existing network diagrams or an internal ticket contact for firewall changes.
3) Infosec to confirm whether an air-gapped (no external control plane) deployment is a hard requirement or a later-stage preference.

Attachments: Redwood_Private_VPC_HighLevel_Architecture.pdf (PDF), ACME_Health_Network_Requirements.xlsx (XLSX)

If helpful I can set a 30-min follow-up with Dev (our SE) to walk through the network spreadsheet with your infra team.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: AcmeHealth private VPC / network & compliance recap

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap and for the attachments. Quick answers from our side:

- PoC stakeholders: myself (product), Bob Chen (platform lead), Anita Rao (infosec lead - infosec@acmehealth.com).
- Preferred PoC window: Aug 17 start would work better given procurement windows.
- Network diagram: attaching the current environment diagram (internal). Our network team prefers to use Private Link-style endpoints; they ask whether Redwood supports either VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink.
- Air gap: Currently a later-stage preference for specific labs; initial PoC can be VPC with strict egress controls.

Infosec questions (Anita copied)
1) Can Redwood run the control-plane in our VPC (private control plane) or do you require any control-plane egress to Redwood-managed endpoints?
2) What data is stored outside the VPC (if anything) and how long is telemetry retained?
3) For KMS: do you support customer-managed keys in KMS/HSM or only Redwood-managed keys?

We'll share the internal network diagram in a separate, internal link for your SE to review.

- Sara

Subject: Re: Post-call: AcmeHealth private VPC / network & compliance recap

Hi Sara / Anita / Bob -

Great - thanks for the fast responses and for confirming the Aug 17 PoC window. Short replies inline to Anita's questions and next steps below.

Anita - answers to your questions:
- Private control plane options: Yes. We offer a private control plane deployment that runs in customer-managed VPCs (private control plane) so there is no outbound internet egress from your environment. For the PoC we can run the control plane in your VPC; we'll provide a lightweight installer and deployment manifest.
- Data stored outside the VPC: By default, short-lived telemetry (health checks, anonymized metrics) may optionally be forwarded to Redwood for platform health; we can turn this off. No customer data or PHI is stored outside the customer VPC unless explicitly configured (and we'll document that).
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS CMKs) and can integrate with HSM-backed keys for encryption-at-rest.

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- Marissa (Redwood): Finalize and send the mutual action plan + PoC SOW by Fri 17 Jul (attached Doc & Drive link).
- Dev (Redwood): 30-min tech sync with Acme network & infra to review ACME_Health_Network_Requirements.xlsx - please propose times; preferably Thu 23 Jul or Fri 24 Jul.
- Anita (Acme): Share the internal network diagram or a link to the internal ticket for firewall changes.
- Laura (Redwood AE): Will initiate procurement intro and share standard PoC contract language / SOW template.

Proposed PoC scope (short):
- Deploy Redwood Private into a dedicated Acme VPC (staging subset).
- Validate 99th percentile latency on 4 representative inference flows and throughput targets (tbd).
- Verify KMS integration and audit log delivery to your log collector.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the tech sync and upload the mutual action plan to the Drive link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME

Thanks again - looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
